data.Name: handle.name
data.Title: handle.name
data.Description:
Dot-separated hierarchical identifier composed of lowercase segments.
Each segment must begin with a lowercase alphabetic character and may
contain lowercase alphanumeric characters with optional internal
hyphen-separated words. Hierarchy is expressed from left to right,
with the most significant component appearing first.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Name: hex.char
data.Title: hex.char
data.Description: Single hexadecimal character. The serialized value must be a string of exactly one ASCII character in 0-9, a-f, or A-F.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Name: left.right.dot
data.Title: left.right.dot
data.Description:
Dot-separated hierarchical identifier composed of lowercase
alphanumeric segments. The first segment must begin with a
lowercase alphabetic character. Subsequent segments may begin
with either a lowercase letter or digit. Hierarchy is expressed
from left to right, with the most significant component appearing first.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Name: market.slot.name
data.Title: market.slot.name
data.Description:
Dot-separated identifier for a specific market slot.
The first segment identifies the market commodity class and MUST be one of `e`, `r`, or `d`. The second segment identifies the market type. The final segment is a 10-digit Unix timestamp in seconds giving the slot start. The middle segments identify the market maker alias and must satisfy the left-right-dot naming rules.
The slot start timestamp MUST align to the duration required by the market type.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Name: non.negative.int
data.Title: non.negative.int
data.Description: Non-negative integer validated non-coercively at the serialized boundary. The serialized value must already be an integer greater than or equal to 0. Strings such as "0" and numeric floats such as 0.0 are not accepted.
data.RawJson: {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0}

data.Name: pascal.case
data.Title: pascal.case
data.Description:
PascalCase identifier composed of ASCII alphanumeric characters.
The first character must be an uppercase alphabetic character.
Separators, whitespace, and underscores are not allowed.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Name: positive.float
data.Title: positive.float
data.Description: Floating-point number strictly greater than zero.
data.RawJson: {"type": "number", "exclusiveMinimum": 0}

data.Name: positive.int
data.Title: positive.int
data.Description: Positive integer validated non-coercively at the serialized boundary. The serialized value must already be an integer greater than 0. Strings such as "1" and numeric floats such as 1.0 are not accepted.
data.RawJson: {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1}

data.Name: spaceheat.name
data.Title: spaceheat.name
data.Description:
Single-segment identifier composed of lowercase alphanumeric
characters with optional internal hyphen-separated words.
Must begin with a lowercase alphabetic character.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Title: utc.iso8601.millis
data.Description: UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format with exactly three digits of fractional seconds (millisecond precision) and a 'Z' suffix.
data.RawJson: {"type": "string"}

data.Title: utc.iso8601.seconds
data.Description: UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format with second precision (no fractional seconds) and a 'Z' suffix.

UTC timestamp expressed as whole milliseconds since the Unix epoch

2000-01-01T00:00:00Z through 3000-01-01T00:00:00Z.

data.Name: utc.seconds

data.Title: analytics.channel.gt
data.Description:
Canonical definition of a computed telemetry channel scoped to a single terminal asset and produced outside SCADA systems.
An analytics.channel.gt declares a computation over message streams, telemetry, or system behavior associated with a specific terminal asset. These channels represent analytics-derived signals such as persistence delay, heartbeat-based health, or other observational metrics.
Unlike derived.channel.gt, analytics.channel.gt is not computed by a GridWorks GNode. Its semantic authority lies in external analytics systems.
data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "`analytics.channel.gt` defines computed telemetry channels whose semantic authority lies outside SCADA systems and whose scope is a single terminal asset.\nValues associated with `analytics.channel.gt` SHALL be represented as floating point numbers, with the unit defined by OutputUnit.\nMulti-terminal-asset computations (e.g. aggregation across assets or GNode-based selection) are intentionally excluded from this type and should be represented by a separate aggregation type."}

data.Title: atn.bid
data.Description:
Legacy market bid submitted by a LeafTransactiveNode for a specific market slot. A bid expresses willingness to inject or withdraw a quantity of the market's commodity as a function of price, subject to the rules of the MarketType associated with the specified MarketSlot.
This type predates the rename of the atomic metered grid actor from AtomicTNode (atn) to LeafTransactiveNode (ltn). It is retained for compatibility with historical messages and is superseded by the bid type, which carries the same contract under a name-neutral vocabulary word.
data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "atn.bid is the original GridWorks market bid message, named when the atomic metered grid actor was called an AtomicTNode (atn). That actor has since been renamed LeafTransactiveNode (ltn), and the bid contract was re-published under the name-neutral vocabulary word bid. New implementations should use bid; atn.bid exists so that historical bids and references such as the ContractId of a market.maker.ack remain interpretable.\nThe structure is unchanged from bid: a single normalized price-quantity curve plus a signed fee transaction. Differences between participant classes are expressed through MarketType rules and authorization registries rather than through specialized bid schemas.\n"}

data.Title: bid
data.Description:
A market-normalized, slot-specific price–quantity schedule submitted by a market participant. A bid expresses willingness to inject or withdraw a quantity of a market-defined commodity as a function of price, subject to the rules of the MarketType associated with the specified MarketSlot.
Bids are economically admissible, cryptographically anchored messages that serve as the primary input to market aggregation and clearing. Differences between participant classes (e.g. leaf nodes, aggregators, fleets, generators) are expressed through MarketType rules and bidder authorization registries, not through differences in bid structure.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "The bid type is the foundational economic message of the GridWorks market architecture. By enforcing strict normalization against MarketType-defined price and quantity domains, bids enable a self-scaling market maker strategy in which aggregation, clearing, and dispatch logic can be applied uniformly across participant classes and market layers.
All bids share a common structure and validation contract. Differences in physical assets, aggregation scope, or operational responsibility are expressed through external registries, MarketType definitions, and settlement processes rather than through specialized bid schemas.
This design supports permissioned or permissionless participation, economic rate-limiting via fees, and bounded computational complexity, while preserving extensibility for future market products and clearing mechanisms.
"}

data.Title: channel.config
data.Description: Base channel configuration used by component definitions to describe how a telemetry channel is sampled, scaled, and serialized.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "`channel.config` captures both periodic sampling behavior and optional asynchronous emission behavior for a telemetry channel.
`PollPeriodMs` and `CapturePeriodS` describe different stages of SCADA behavior. `PollPeriodMs` is the cadence at which SCADA polls the hardware device or upstream source for a value. `CapturePeriodS` is the cadence at which SCADA emits that channel value into the telemetry stream.
These cadences may differ. For example, SCADA may poll a device frequently to maintain fresh local state while only reporting the value periodically or when an async trigger condition is met.
In current runtime practice, `AsyncCapture` may be true even when `AsyncCaptureDelta` is omitted. This means asynchronous capture is enabled, but the threshold semantics are not fully specified in the payload itself.
When `AsyncCaptureDelta` is present, the intended interpretation is: publish asynchronously when the magnitude of the change since the last published value is greater than or equal to `AsyncCaptureDelta`.
`Exponent` describes how to interpret the serialized integer reading relative to `Unit`. For example, if `Unit` is `Gpm` and `Exponent` is `2`, then a reading value of `432` represents `4.32 Gpm`.
A future published version may strengthen this contract by requiring `AsyncCaptureDelta` whenever `AsyncCapture` is true, once runtime behavior consistently provides that value.
"}

data.Title: connectivity.edge.gt
data.Description:
Directed topological edge connecting two Grid Nodes (GNodes) in the physical electric network. This type encodes copper-level adjacency used for graph-based modeling, Kirchhoff power flow calculations, and constraint propagation.
A ConnectivityEdge represents an oriented structural relationship between two distinct GNodes. Direction SHALL be interpreted as the positive reference direction for flow modeling and graph traversal. Physical power MAY flow in either direction subject to system conditions.
For a given pair of GNodes, only one structural ConnectivityEdge SHALL exist. Reverse flow SHALL be represented by sign conventions in power quantities and SHALL NOT be modeled by introducing a secondConnectivityEdge reversing the same GNode pair.
ConnectivityEdge does not encode electrical impedance, capacity, or switching state. It defines structural topology only.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "ConnectivityEdge represents structural conductor adjacency only. Most edges correspond directly to parent–child relationships in the GNode hierarchy (for example, substation to feeder or feeder to downstream connectivity node). In these cases, the directed edge makes explicit the physical copper relationship already implied by the structural topology.
However, real distribution systems may contain tie-lines, loops, and alternate routing paths. The graph formed by ConnectivityEdge objects MAY therefore contain cycles. Acyclicity is not assumed.
The directed orientation of a ConnectivityEdge establishes a positive reference direction for flow modeling and graph traversal. It does NOT restrict physical power flow to a single direction. Reverse flow SHALL be represented by sign conventions in power quantities rather than by duplicating edges in the opposite direction.
Status expresses lifecycle participation of the edge in the registry and coordination system. It SHALL NOT be interpreted as operational switching state (e.g., breaker open or closed). Operational configuration of the active network graph MUST be modeled using separate types designed for dynamic topology state.
Conceptually, ConnectivityEdge aligns with the conductor adjacency relationships represented in IEC 61970/61968 CIM (Common Information Model), where network topology is derived from connections between ConnectivityNodes through conducting equipment. ConnectivityEdge provides a simplified, distribution-level abstraction suitable for graph-based modeling and transactive coordination without adopting the full CIM equipment hierarchy."}

data.Title: data.channel.gt
data.Description:

A data.channel.gt declares the semantic identity of a telemetry stream, including what is measured, which node it describes, and which node captures the measurement. To interpret a channel.readings instance, consumers SHALL resolve ChannelName against the channel definitions for the relevant terminal asset / SCADA context (typically by matching data.channel.gt.Name).
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "data.channel.gt defines primary telemetry channels corresponding to directly observed measurements from physical devices or sensors.

data.Description:

data.Title: flo.params.house0
data.Description: Complete input parameter set for one run of the Forward Looking Optimization (FLO) algorithm against a House0 thermal model. It captures the optimization horizon, the modeled equipment, the initial state of thermal storage, the price and weather forecasts, and the house thermal-response coefficients needed to plan heat pump operation and produce a market bid.
data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "A LeafTransactiveNode builds a flo.params.house0 each market slot to drive its Forward Looking Optimization. FLO models the home's heat pump and thermal storage over HorizonHours, searches for the lowest-cost operating plan against the price and weather forecasts, and from that plan derives the price-quantity curve the node submits as its market bid.\nThe parameters fall into groups: identity and timing (GNodeAlias, FloParamsUid, TimezoneStr, StartUnixS, ParamsGeneratedS, FloAlias, FloGitCommit); horizon and storage geometry (HorizonHours, NumLayers, StorageVolumeGallons, StorageLossesPercent); heat pump characteristics (HpMinElecKw, HpMaxElecKw, HpTurnOnMinutes, HpIsOff, and the Cop terms); the initial thermal state (the InitialTemp and InitialThermocline fields, BufferAvailableKwh, HouseAvailableKwh); the forecasts and their provenance ids; and the House0 thermal-response coefficients and operating points (Alpha/Beta/Gamma, the Intermediate and Dd fields, MaxEwtF). Several coefficients are carried as scaled integers to keep the serialized contract free of floating point representation.\nVersion 003 was emitted by the SCADA codebase in two shapes, because a field was added without bumping the version. The original shape (the \"Winter.Oak\" runs, 2025-04 through 2025-09) carries FloAlias and FloGitCommit and no ConstantDeltaT. A later shape (2025-11) carries ConstantDeltaT and drops FloAlias and FloGitCommit. All three of those fields are therefore optional in this schema, while the remaining properties are common to both shapes with identical types. A valid v003 message matches exactly one of the two historical shapes; this schema accepts both."}

data.Title: g.node.gt
data.Description: A GNode (“Grid Node”) is the fundamental identity object in the GridWorks  ecosystem. Every physical location, metered unit, device, service, or actor  interacting with the transactive system is represented as a GNode.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "Grid Nodes (GNodes) provide the stable identity layer for distributed coordination in the GridWorks ecosystem. Each GNode participates in a hierarchical alias structure that encodes topology, routing semantics, and coordination scope.
GNodes may represent physical grid structure (e.g., metered boundaries, connectivity nodes, constraint points) or logical and service roles (e.g., SCADA agents, forecasting services, market participants). BaseClass defines the universal structural ontology required for interoperability. GNodeClass expresses organization-specific functional roles and does not alter structural semantics.
`g.node.gt` is an immutable serialized snapshot of declared node state. Any change to a GNode (alias updates, status changes, relocations, or classification changes) SHALL be represented by publishing a new `g.node.gt` message rather than mutating a previously published instance. This preserves durable identity (GNodeId) while allowing controlled evolution of descriptive attributes.
GNode is designed as the atomic unit of coordination in a recursively composable grid architecture. Systems of arbitrary scale are formed by composing GNodes into hierarchical or heterarchical structures. This allows optimal power flow (OPF), market clearing, and constraint coordination mechanisms to operate centrally, regionally, or in distributed configurations without altering the underlying identity model.
Conceptually, GNode aligns with node abstractions in IEC 61970/61968 CIM (e.g., ConnectivityNode and TopologicalNode), while unifying physical and logical coordination entities within a single identity abstraction suitable for graph-based modeling and transactive coordination.
"}

data.Title: g.node.instance.gt

data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "The g.node.instance.gt type represents a durable record of runtime authority for a Grid Node. It is maintained by the Fleet Index Service (FIS) and serves as an auditable snapshot of instance lifecycle events.

data.Title: linear.one.dimensional.calibration
data.Description:
Linear calibration applied to a measurement expressed in the derived channel's declared OutputUnit domain.
The transformation is interpreted as:

    calibrated = M * x + B

where:

  - x is the input measurement first converted into the OutputUnit
    scaling of the derived channel.

data.Title: new.command.tree

data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "A GridWorks SCADA node owns the hardware layout and the actor hierarchy that commands it. When that hierarchy changes -- for example when control is handed between automatic and administrative bosses -- the SCADA node sends a new.command.tree to its LeafTransactiveNode so the LTN's view of who commands whom stays current.\nThe message is a full snapshot rather than a delta: the recipient discards its previous command tree and adopts ShNodes as the new one. data.Title: position.point.gt

data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "PositionPoint represents the physical location of a GNode that has spatial meaning within the electric grid, such as TerminalAssets, LeafTransactiveNodes, MarketMaker constraint points, and ConnectivityNodes. Coordinates are expressed in WGS84 (EPSG:4326), the standard global geodetic reference system used by GPS and commonly adopted in utility GIS, mapping, and DERMS integrations.\nThis type corresponds to a simplified form of the IEC 61970/61968 CIM `PositionPoint` class. The CIM model supports elevation, coordinate-system definitions, and collections of points for geometric shapes. GridWorks intentionally restricts this type to a single latitude/longitude pair to provide a deterministic and minimal spatial anchor for coordination.\nPosition accuracy is not prescribed by this type. The microdegree representation provides sufficient precision to distinguish distribution-level assets (e.g., residential footprints, poles, transformers, substations). data.Title: report
data.Description: Primary telemetry and state reporting message produced by a SCADA node for a specific reporting slot. A report contains all meaningful channel readings, state transitions, and FSM outputs observed during the slot period.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "Reports are sent at fixed slot intervals (typically 5 minutes) and provide a durable historical record of telemetry and state changes observed during that period.
GridWorks SCADA devices emit most channel readings asynchronously when values change beyond configured thresholds. Each reading is timestamped at the moment of observation by the SCADA device. Reports preserve these original timestamps without resampling or aggregation.
As a result, a report represents a batched event log for the slot period rather than a sampled snapshot. Consumers can reconstruct the precise timing of state transitions (e.g., relay changes) and value updates within the slot window.
This differs from snapshot messages, which represent the most recent value of each channel at a single point in time and are optimized for near-real-time visualization rather than historical accuracy.
"}

data.Title: scada.params
data.Description: Message used to read or change the HA1 control parameters held by a SCADA node, exchanged between a LeafTransactiveNode and a SCADA node. A request carries the proposed NewParams; the SCADA node's reply echoes the same MessageId and reports the parameters in effect before and after the change.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "HA1 is the home-heating control algorithm run by a GridWorks SCADA node. scada.params is the boundary message for inspecting and updating the algorithm's tuning parameters without redeploying the SCADA node.
The exchange is request/reply. A LeafTransactiveNode sends a scada.params with NewParams set to the parameters it wants applied. The SCADA node adopts them, then replies with a scada.params that echoes the request's MessageId, sets OldParams to the values it had been running, and sets NewParams to the values now in effect. A request with NewParams absent reads the current parameters without changing them. NewParams and OldParams are optional because not every message in the exchange carries both.
The SCADA codebase held scada.params at version 004 across an ha1.params version bump, so version 004 messages were emitted carrying either an ha1.params version 004 or version 005 object. NewParams and OldParams therefore accept both, expressed as a oneOf of those two ha1.params versions; the ha1.params Version field discriminates which one a given message carries.
"}

data.Title: synced.readings.bundle
data.Description:
Time-aligned sequence of synchronized multi-channel readings with embedded channel semantics sufficient for independent interpretation.
For each channel, values in its associated ValueList are ordered to align by index with TimestampList, such that the value at index i corresponds to TimestampList[i].
ChannelDefinitions provides the measurement unit required to interpret values for each channel.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "
`synced.readings.bundle` represents a rectangular, time-aligned dataset across multiple channels.
ChannelName values are identifiers defined within a GridWorks SCADA layout context (e.g. layout.lite or gw.nolan.layout). They are not globally standardized vocabulary and SHALL be interpreted only within the context in which they were produced.
ChannelDefinitions provides a minimal projection of channel semantics, including `Name`, `Id`, `Unit` and `UnitType`, sufficient to interpret the numeric values in this bundle without requiring access to the full layout.
The `Id` together with the channel TypeName (e.g. `data.channel.gt`, `derived.channel.gt`, or `analytics.channel.gt`) enables resolution of the authoritative channel definition. This bundle is not a source of semantic authority; it provides a convenient projection for transport, indexing, and querying.
In GridWorks systems, full channel definitions are typically available in layout artifacts such as `layout.lite`, which include additional information such as `AboutNodeName`, `CapturedByNodeName`, and derivation strategy. Those details are intentionally omitted here to keep this type lightweight and focused on boundary interpretation.
All channels share a common `TimestampList`. For any index i, values across all channels correspond to the same point in time.
"}

data.Title: ticklist.hall
data.Description: A batch of tick timestamps captured from a hall-effect flow meter by its pico flow module, as posted by the pico to a SCADA node. Each tick marks one revolution-equivalent pulse of the meter. Tick times are given as microsecond offsets from an absolute first-tick timestamp.
data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "ticklist.hall is the raw pico-to-SCADA payload in GridWorks' experiments with hall-effect flow meters. A pico flow module attached to the meter accumulates ticks and HTTP-posts them in batches to the SCADA node's flow module actor, which reconstructs absolute tick times by adding each RelativeMicrosecondList offset to FirstTickTimestampNanoSecond and applying the clock-offset correction derived from PicoBeforePostTimestampNanoSecond.\nThe SCADA node wraps this payload, together with channel and terminal asset context, in a ticklist.hall.report for forwarding to the LeafTransactiveNode. The reed-switch counterpart is ticklist.reed, which differs in tick-offset resolution because reed switches actuate far more slowly than hall sensors.\n"}

data.Title: ticklist.hall.report
data.Description: A hall-effect flow meter tick batch (ticklist.hall) wrapped by a SCADA node with the channel and terminal asset context needed to interpret it, for forwarding to the LeafTransactiveNode.

A pico flow module posts a raw ticklist.hall to the SCADA node's flow module actor; when tick list publishing is enabled, that actor wraps the payload with terminal asset, channel, and receive-time context and sends this report to the LeafTransactiveNode. The reed-switch counterpart is ticklist.reed.report.\n"}

data.Title: weather.forecast
data.Description: A multi-interval outside-air-temperature and wind-speed forecast for a geographic location, as fetched by a SCADA node from a third-party weather service. Each forecast interval has an entry in the parallel Time, OatF, and WindSpeedMph lists.
data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "weather.forecast carries raw forecast data obtained directly from a third-party weather service. In the SCADA codebase it is produced by the derived-data actor, which fetches an hourly forecast from the National Weather Service (api.weather.gov) for an ICAO weather station, falling back to the coldest historical temperature for the current month when no forecast is available. The actor uses the forecast to compute heating forecasts (required power and source water temperature) and sends the forecast to the LeafTransactiveNode for record-keeping.\nGridWorks plans to introduce a dedicated weather forecast service (and a parallel price forecast service) that publishes to broadcast channels GNodes can subscribe to, rather than each node fetching weather on its own. weather.forecast is the message such a service would broadcast.\n"}

schema.name: HasBindings
schema.Description: TRUE iff at least one FeatureBindings row points at this feature. Distinguishes 'shipped' (has bindings) from 'planned' (no bindings yet) — without a separate state column.

data.Name: snapshot_pipeline
data.Summary: Restrict + expand a seed YAML and emit a runnable Python SDK snapshot.
data.Description: Two CLI verbs (`sema snapshot prepare` and `sema snapshot build`) drive a pipeline that takes a structured seed-request YAML, computes the transitive closure of the requested types/enums/formats, writes restricted definitions and indexes under output/sema/, and finally generates Python runtime files keyed by --package-name. Models the snapshot pieces tracked in SeedRequests / Snapshots / LocalNames.

data.Name: reverse_dependencies
data.Summary: Show transitive reverse dependencies for a Sema word.
data.Description: The `sema reverse <name> [version]` command resolves a Sema word and walks the reverse-dependency closure, returning every dependent type/enum/format. For types and enums the version is required; for formats it's omitted.

data.Name: axiom_template_enforcement
data.Summary: Every published version with declared axioms MUST have a Jinja axiom template.
data.Description: Per commit 87bbeef, runtime generation FAILS if a schema declares an axiom without a corresponding template. `sema runtime scaffold-axiom-template` creates the missing stub. Templates live under src/sema/tools/runtime_generation/templates/axioms/ and are modeled in the rulebook's Templates table (Tier A5).

data.Name: upgrade_template_enforcement
data.Summary: Every upgrade hop must have a Jinja upgrade template.
data.Description: Companion to axiom_template_enforcement. `sema runtime scaffold-upgrade-template <type> <ver> <next>` creates the stub for an outgoing version. Templates live under src/sema/tools/runtime_generation/templates/upgrades/.

data.Name: yaml_round_trip
data.Summary: Rulebook ⇄ YAML parity: emit YAML from the rulebook and re-import it without loss.
data.Description: rulebook-emitters/yaml/ provides the emit-and-reimport pair (rulebook_to_yaml.py + yaml_to_rulebook.py) plus yaml_round_trip_check.py to assert canonical equivalence. Currently ~97% round-trip parity.

data.Name: magic_links_auth
data.Summary: Passwordless email-code authentication for the sema admin surface.
data.Description: The single AppUsers row in the rulebook + the auth.trusted_tenants seeding in init-db.sh + the .secrets/sema-tenant.json file together implement magic-links auth for the bases.effortlessapi.com tenant. Standard ERB add-on via the effortless-magic-links skill.

data.Name: postgres_codegen
data.Summary: Compile the rulebook into a runnable Postgres database (tables, functions, views).
data.Description: The rulebook-to-postgres transpiler reads effortless-rulebook.json and emits postgres/01-05*.sql. init-db.sh runs them in order against a local Postgres. 02b and similar `*b-customize-*.sql` files hold hand-written overrides for cases the transpiler can't yet express.

data.Name: public_registry_index
data.Summary: Publishable surface: types/enums/formats with at least one published version.
data.Description: build_public_registry.py reads definitions/registry.yaml and emits indexes/public_registry.yaml, including only published-version rows. In rulebook terms the same membership is `vw_types WHERE published_version_count > 0` (and analogous for enums/formats). Tracked as an IndexBuilders row, not a calculated field on the schema-of-record (see plan §A2 SUBSUMED).

FeatureBindings.Description: Many-to-many resolution rows linking a Feature to the concrete pieces that implement it: CliCommands, Emitters, IndexBuilders, Templates, rulebook tables, etc. Kind is the discriminator; TargetName names the row inside the bound catalog. Notes is free-form.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Compound key: <Feature>::<Kind>::<TargetName>. Auto-derived.

schema.name: Feature
schema.Description: FK to the Features row.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: One of 'cli', 'emitter', 'index', 'template', 'table'. Tells the consumer which catalog to look TargetName up in.

schema.name: TargetName
schema.Description: Name of the bound row inside its catalog. For example, Kind='cli' / TargetName='sema snapshot prepare'; Kind='emitter' / TargetName='yaml'; Kind='table' / TargetName='SeedRequests'.

schema.name: Notes
schema.Description: Free-form annotation about why this binding exists or any caveat.

data.Notes: Index builder under src/sema/tools/; the CLI loads its output.
Templates rows with Kind='axiom' gate the build.
